question: Building sandstone crushes under 40,000 kilonewtons per square metre and weighs 20 per cubic metre. How tall, in km, could a column rise?
move: When a strong structure fails, suspect its shape before its material.
trap: Guessing a few hundred metres, as if cathedrals strained their stone.
hint: Each metre of height adds 20 kilonewtons on every square metre of the base.
steps: Each metre of column adds 20 kN on each square metre of its base.
simply: Stack 2,000 one-metre cubes of sandstone: only then does the bottom cube begin to crush. The highest Gothic vault, at Beauvais, is 48 m.
source: Heyman, Ingenia, Royal Academy of Engineering
